objects.description: Character unit used by the library. It is either a UTF-16 WCHAR on Windows when MD4C_USE_UTF16 is defined during both build and use, or a narrow char otherwise. Used for all text passed into and out of the API.
Unsigned integer type representing sizes/lengths for MD4C APIs. Width matches unsigned. Use for buffer sizes and counts.
Unsigned integer type representing offsets into input buffers. Width matches unsigned.

objects.description: Enumeration of block-level Markdown nodes emitted by the parser via enter_block/leave_block callbacks. Values identify document, quote, lists, headers, code blocks, raw HTML, paragraph, and table-related blocks.

objects.definition:
typedef enum MD_SPANTYPE {
    MD_SPAN_EM,
    MD_SPAN_STRONG,
    MD_SPAN_A,
    MD_SPAN_IMG,
    MD_SPAN_CODE,
    MD_SPAN_DEL,
    MD_SPAN_LATEXMATH,
    MD_SPAN_LATEXMATH_DISPLAY,
    MD_SPAN_WIKILINK,
    MD_SPAN_U
} MD_SPANTYPE;
objects.description: Enumeration of inline span types emitted by the parser via enter_span/leave_span callbacks, covering emphasis, strong, links, images, code, deletion, LaTeX math, wiki links, and underline.
Enumeration of text fragment types delivered to the text callback: normal text, replacement for NUL, hard/soft breaks, entities, code text, raw HTML text, and LaTeX math text.
Enumeration for table cell alignment used in table details.

Structured string attribute carrying a non–zero-terminated text with segmentation metadata (types and offsets of substrings). Used for attributes such as link href/title, image src/title, etc. substr_offsets[0]==0 and substr_offsets[last+1]==size are guaranteed.
Detail struct passed for MD_BLOCK_UL blocks: indicates tight/loose list and bullet character used in source ('-','+','*').
Detail struct for MD_BLOCK_OL: start index, tight/loose, and delimiter character for list numbers ('.' or ')').
Detail struct for MD_BLOCK_LI: task list metadata if enabled (is_task, task mark char, and its input offset).
Detail struct for MD_BLOCK_H: header level 1–6.
Detail struct for MD_BLOCK_CODE: info string, extracted language, and the fence character used (or 0 for indented code).
Detail struct for MD_BLOCK_TABLE: table dimensions (column count, header/body row counts).
Detail struct for MD_BLOCK_TH/MD_BLOCK_TD: alignment for the cell.
Detail struct for MD_SPAN_A: link href and title attributes (segmented), and whether it is an autolink.
Detail struct for MD_SPAN_IMG: image source and title attributes (segmented).
Detail struct for MD_SPAN_WIKILINK: wiki link target attribute. Note: the tag name in the typedef differs (struct MD_SPAN_WIKILINK) while the typedef name is MD_SPAN_WIKILINK_DETAIL.

Top-level parser configuration passed to md_parse. Holds ABI version, dialect flags, and callback function pointers for blocks, spans, text, and optional debug logging. syntax is reserved and must be NULL. Fields without otherwise noted must be initialized (abi_version=0, syntax=NULL) per the comments.

functions.name: md_parse
functions.signature: int md_parse(const MD_CHAR* text, MD_SIZE size, const MD_PARSER* parser, void* userdata);
functions.description: Parses a Markdown document from the buffer 'text' of length 'size' (in MD_CHAR units) and drives the supplied MD_PARSER callbacks to render or process the document. Returns 0 on success; returns -1 on internal runtime error; or returns a non-zero value propagated from a callback if a callback aborts parsing by returning non-zero. Strings provided to callbacks are generally not zero-terminated; sizes must be honored. Use when you need structured parsing with custom callbacks rather than HTML rendering.
requirements: text must point to a readable buffer containing at least 'size' MD_CHARs.
size is the number of MD_CHAR code units in 'text'. It may be zero to parse an empty document (behavior otherwise unspecified beyond normal parsing).
parser must be a valid pointer to an initialized MD_PARSER structure.
parser->abi_version must be set to 0 (reserved).
parser->flags is a bitmask of MD_FLAG_* values defined in md4c.h.
parser->debug_log is optional and may be NULL; if non-NULL it may receive diagnostic messages.
parser->syntax must be set to NULL (reserved).

Callbacks enter_block, leave_block, enter_span, leave_span, and text must match the declared signatures. The header does not state they are optional; if provided, they must tolerate being called with non-null detail pointers appropriate to the type.
Any string arguments delivered to callbacks (including members of detail structures) are generally not zero-terminated; callback implementations must use the provided size values.
Any rendering callback may abort parsing by returning non-zero; callers must be prepared for md_parse() to return that non-zero value and handle it appropriately.
userdata is passed through to callbacks and may be NULL.
If MD4C_USE_UTF16 is used, both the MD4C library and the including code must be compiled with MD4C_USE_UTF16 defined (Windows-only).

functions.name: md_html
functions.signature: int md_html(const MD_CHAR* input, MD_SIZE input_size, void (*process_output)(const MD_CHAR*, MD_SIZE, void*), void* userdata, unsigned parser_flags, unsigned renderer_flags);
functions.description: Parses Markdown from 'input' of length 'input_size' and renders the body as HTML, delivering output in chunks to the 'process_output' callback. Only the HTML body is produced; callers should add their own HTML header/footer. Returns 0 on success; returns -1 on error (if md_parse fails internally). Use when you need Markdown-to-HTML conversion via a callback that consumes output chunks.
requirements: input must point to a readable buffer containing at least 'input_size' MD_CHARs.
input_size is the number of MD_CHAR code units in 'input'.

process_output must be a non-NULL function matching the signature void(const MD_CHAR*, MD_SIZE, void*); it will be called zero or more times with non-zero-terminated chunks of output and must honor the supplied size.
process_output must not assume the chunk strings are zero-terminated; it must use the provided size.
userdata is passed through to process_output and may be NULL.
parser_flags is a bitmask of MD_FLAG_* values defined in md4c.h; these are forwarded to md_parse().
renderer_flags is a bitmask of MD_HTML_FLAG_* values; MD_HTML_FLAG_DEBUG sends md_parse() debug output to stderr; other flags control entity handling, BOM skipping, and XHTML output.
If MD4C_USE_UTF16 is used, both the MD4C library and the including code must be compiled with MD4C_USE_UTF16 defined (Windows-only).
Caller must handle the return value: 0 indicates success; -1 indicates an error occurred during parsing/rendering.

endpoints.name: md_parse
md_html

data_types.description: A text buffer containing Markdown source. May include headings, lists, code fences, blockquotes, links, images, inline emphasis, raw HTML fragments, tables, and other Markdown constructs. The data is treated as a sequence of character units (MD_CHAR), not necessarily null-terminated, and may contain arbitrary bytes; the parser consumes exactly the provided length.

generators.generator:
import random
import string
from typing import List

# Generator for valid, interesting Markdown inputs for md4c-based fuzzers.
# Focus: produce syntactically valid Markdown covering many constructs: headings,
# lists (UL/OL, tight/loose, task lists), blockquotes, code fences/indented code,
# links/images (with titles), autolinks, emphasis/strong/u/del, HTML blocks, tables,
# entities, line breaks, and LaTeX spans where applicable. Keep total size <= 4096 bytes.

MAX_BYTES = 4096

# Small helper pools
ALPHANUM = string.ascii_letters + string.digits
PUNCT = "-_./:?#[]@!$&'()*+,;="
URL_SCHEMES = [
    "http://", "https://", "mailto:", "tel:", "ftp://", "file://",
]
IMG_EXTS = ["png", "jpg", "jpeg", "gif", "svg"]
LANGS = ["c", "cpp", "python", "javascript", "json", "xml", "bash", "html", "markdown"]
UL_MARKS = ["-", "+", "*"]
OL_DELIMS = [".", ")"]
ENTITIES = ["&", "<", ">", """, "©", "©"]
EMPH_PAIRS = [("*", "*"), ("_", "_"), ("~", "~"), ("__", "__"), ("**", "**")]
U_PAIRS = [("<u>", "</u>")]  # underline via HTML tag (md4c supports MD_SPAN_U)


def r_word(r: random.Random, min_len=3, max_len=10) -> str:
    n = r.randint(min_len, max_len)
    return ''.join(r.choice(ALPHANUM) for _ in range(n))


def r_text(r: random.Random, words=5, extra_punct=True) -> str:
    parts = []
    for _ in range(words):
        w = r_word(r)
        if extra_punct and r.random() < 0.3:
            w += r.choice([",", ":", ";", "...", "!"])
        parts.append(w)
    return ' '.join(parts)


def mk_heading(r: random.Random) -> str:
    level = r.randint(1, 6)
    title = r_text(r, words=r.randint(2, 6))
    # Occasionally add trailing hashes per CommonMark allowance
    trailer = ''
    if r.random() < 0.4:
        trailer = ' ' + ('#' * level)
    return f"{'#' * level} {title}{trailer}\n\n"


def mk_blockquote(r: random.Random) -> str:
    lines = []
    for _ in range(r.randint(1, 3)):
        lines.append("> " + r_text(r, words=r.randint(4, 10)))
    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n\n"


def mk_ulist(r: random.Random, tight: bool | None = None) -> str:
    if tight is None:
        tight = r.random() < 0.5
    mark = r.choice(UL_MARKS)
    items = []
    for i in range(r.randint(2, 5)):
        line = f"{mark} " + r_text(r, words=r.randint(3, 8))
        # Optional task list syntax
        if r.random() < 0.5:
            task_mark = "x" if r.random() < 0.5 else " "
            line = f"{mark} [{task_mark}] " + r_text(r, words=r.randint(2, 6))
        items.append(line)
        # Nested list or paragraph to vary tight/loose
        if r.random() < 0.3:
            sub = f"  {mark} " + r_text(r, words=r.randint(2,5))
            items.append(sub)
        if not tight and r.random() < 0.5:
            items.append("")
    return "\n".join(items) + "\n\n"


def mk_olist(r: random.Random, tight: bool | None = None) -> str:
    if tight is None:
        tight = r.random() < 0.5
    start = r.randint(1, 4) if r.random() < 0.5 else 1
    delim = r.choice(OL_DELIMS)
    items = []
    cur = start
    for _ in range(r.randint(2, 5)):
        items.append(f"{cur}{delim} " + r_text(r, words=r.randint(3, 8)))
        cur += 1
        if not tight and r.random() < 0.5:
            items.append("")
    return "\n".join(items) + "\n\n"


def mk_codeblock(r: random.Random) -> str:
    if r.random() < 0.5:
        # fenced
        fence_char = r.choice(['`', '~'])
        fence_len = r.randint(3, 5)
        fence = fence_char * fence_len
        info = ''
        if r.random() < 0.7:
            lang = r.choice(LANGS)
            # Add info string extras
            extra = ''
            if r.random() < 0.5:
                extra = ' ' + r_text(r, words=r.randint(1, 3), extra_punct=False)
            info = ' ' + lang + extra
        lines = []
        for _ in range(r.randint(2, 6)):
            # Avoid accidentally closing fence by mixing characters
            line = ''.join(r.choice(string.printable.replace(fence_char, '')) for _ in range(r.randint(10, 40)))
            lines.append(line.rstrip())
        return f"{fence}{info}\n" + "\n".join(lines) + f"\n{fence}\n\n"
    else:
        # indented code block
        lines = []
        for _ in range(r.randint(2, 5)):
            lines.append("    " + ''.join(r.choice(string.printable) for _ in range(r.randint(8, 30))).rstrip())
        return "\n".join(lines) + "\n\n"


def mk_link(r: random.Random) -> str:
    label = r_text(r, words=r.randint(1, 3), extra_punct=False)
    # Occasionally include nested emphasis inside label
    if r.random() < 0.4:
        em_open, em_close = r.choice(EMPH_PAIRS)
        label = f"{em_open}{label}{em_close}"
    url = r.choice(URL_SCHEMES) + r_word(r, 3, 8)
    if r.random() < 0.7:
        url += '/' + r_word(r, 3, 8)
    if r.random() < 0.4:
        url += '?' + r_word(r, 3, 6) + '=' + r_word(r, 2, 5)
    title = ''
    if r.random() < 0.6:
        q = '"' if r.random() < 0.5 else "'"
        title = f" {q}{r_text(r, words=r.randint(2,5))}{q}"
    return f"[{label}]({url}{title})"


def mk_image(r: random.Random) -> str:
    alt = r_text(r, words=r.randint(1, 3), extra_punct=False)
    src = r.choice(URL_SCHEMES) + r_word(r, 3, 7) + '.' + r.choice(IMG_EXTS)
    title = ''
    if r.random() < 0.5:
        q = '"' if r.random() < 0.5 else "'"
        title = f" {q}{r_text(r, words=r.randint(1,3))}{q}"
    return f"![{alt}]({src}{title})"


def mk_paragraph(r: random.Random) -> str:
    bits: List[str] = []
    n = r.randint(5, 12)
    for _ in range(n):
        choice = r.random()
        if choice < 0.15:
            bits.append(mk_link(r))
        elif choice < 0.25:
            bits.append(mk_image(r))
        elif choice < 0.45:
            # emphasis variants
            em_open, em_close = r.choice(EMPH_PAIRS)
            bits.append(f"{em_open}{r_text(r, words=r.randint(1,3))}{em_close}")
        elif choice < 0.55:
            # underline via HTML tag
            uo, uc = U_PAIRS[0]
            bits.append(f"{uo}{r_text(r, words=r.randint(1,3))}{uc}")
        elif choice < 0.65:
            # inline code
            backticks = '`' * r.randint(1, 2)
            content = r_text(r, words=r.randint(1,3), extra_punct=False)
            if backticks in content:
                content = content.replace('`', '')
            bits.append(f"{backticks}{content}{backticks}")
        elif choice < 0.75:
            bits.append(r.choice(ENTITIES))
        elif choice < 0.85:
            # autolink
            bits.append('<' + r.choice(URL_SCHEMES) + r_word(r, 3, 8) + '>')
        else:
            bits.append(r_text(r, words=1))
    # Insert hard/soft breaks
    joiner = '  \n' if r.random() < 0.5 else '\n'
    return ' '.join(bits) + f"\n\n"


def mk_html_block(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Simple HTML block (comment or tag)
    if r.random() < 0.5:
        return f"<!-- {r_text(r, words=r.randint(3,8))} -->\n\n"
    else:
        tag = r.choice(["div", "span", "script", "style", "blockquote"])  # md4c handles appropriately
        attrs = ''
        if r.random() < 0.6:
            attrs = f" class=\"{r_word(r,3,8)}\" id=\"{r_word(r,4,10)}\""
        inner = r_text(r, words=r.randint(3,10))
        return f"<{tag}{attrs}>{inner}</{tag}>\n\n"


def mk_table(r: random.Random) -> str:
    cols = r.randint(2, 5)
    headers = [r_word(r, 3, 8).title() for _ in range(cols)]
    # Alignment row
    aligns = []
    for _ in range(cols):
        a = r.random()
        if a < 0.33:
            aligns.append(":" + "-" * r.randint(3,5))  # left
        elif a < 0.66:
            aligns.append(":" + "-" * r.randint(3,5) + ":")  # center
        else:
            aligns.append("-" * r.randint(3,5) + ":")  # right
    rows = []
    for _ in range(r.randint(2, 5)):
        row = []
        for _c in range(cols):
            choice = r.random()
            if choice < 0.2:
                row.append(mk_link(r))
            elif choice < 0.35:
                row.append(mk_image(r))
            else:
                row.append(r_text(r, words=r.randint(1,3)))
        rows.append(" | ".join(row))
    table = [" | ".join(headers), "|".join(aligns)] + rows
    return "\n".join(table) + "\n\n"


def mk_math_spans(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Inline and display math fenced by $ or $$ (md4c has LATEXMATH types)
    inline = f"$ {r_text(r, words=r.randint(1,3), extra_punct=False)} $"
    display = f"$$ {r_text(r, words=r.randint(2,4), extra_punct=False)} $$"
    return inline + "\n\n" + display + "\n\n"


def assemble_document(r: random.Random, target_size: int) -> str:
    sections = []
    makers = [
        mk_heading,
        mk_blockquote,
        mk_ulist,
        mk_olist,
        mk_codeblock,
        mk_paragraph,
        mk_html_block,
        mk_table,
        mk_math_spans,
    ]
    # Start with a heading to set structure
    sections.append(mk_heading(r))
    # Add a mix until close to target size
    while True:
        maker = r.choice(makers)
        piece = maker(r) if maker not in (mk_ulist, mk_olist) else maker(r, tight=None)
        sections.append(piece)
        doc = ''.join(sections)
        if len(doc.encode('utf-8', errors='ignore')) > target_size:
            break
        if len(sections) > 20 and r.random() < 0.3:
            break
    # Ensure trailing newline
    doc = ''.join(sections)
    if not doc.endswith('\n'):
        doc += '\n'
    return doc


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)
    # Choose a target size below MAX_BYTES; reserve headroom for UTF-8 encoding length variation
    target = r.randint(512, min(3000, MAX_BYTES))
    doc = assemble_document(r, target)
    # md4c treats input as MD_CHAR units; our fuzz harness copies raw bytes.
    # Return as UTF-8 bytes (valid, common). Keep <= MAX_BYTES.
    data = doc.encode('utf-8')
    if len(data) > MAX_BYTES:
        data = data[:MAX_BYTES]
        # Ensure we don't cut multi-byte sequence: find safe cut
        try:
            data.decode('utf-8')
        except UnicodeDecodeError:
            # Back off to previous valid boundary
            for i in range(len(data) - 1, 0, -1):
                try:
                    data[:i].decode('utf-8')
                    data = data[:i]
                    break
                except UnicodeDecodeError:
                    continue
    return data
